_doc: Reveal assets deliberately kept on disk while unreferenced. Read by tools/validate-reveal-assets.mjs. EXACT paths only — no globs, no wildcards, no directories. An unreferenced file that is NOT listed here fails the gate; that is the point. Adding an entry is a decision, and the reason field is where the decision is recorded. The gate also fails if an entry stops existing or becomes referenced again, so this file cannot silently rot.

_status.superseded: Replaced by better artwork. Kept because deleting a lesson image is not a QA decision — see the reason for what replaced it and when.
_status.unwired: Artwork that exists but no lesson references. Awaiting an authoring decision on whether to wire it or retire it. NOT a licence to leave it forever.

retained.reason: A stock photograph of a teacher and students, on a lesson about mean absolute deviation. It carried no data at all and matched neither its own Notice & Wonder prompt nor the lesson's basketball scenario. Replaced by notice-wonder.svg, a forecast-highs chart with the mean drawn in.

A byte-identical copy of 4-4's battery icons. 4-3's prompt, launch narrative and Connect check all describe a 6 GB phone, so the lesson was showing its neighbour's picture. Replaced by notice-wonder.svg, the storage bar the prompt describes.
A byte-identical copy of 7-8's polygon flower. 7-7's prompt describes a town-planning grid with two surveyed park corners. Replaced by notice-wonder.svg, that grid.

A Book Fair attendance table (Mon 55, Tue 80, Wed 70, Thu 112, Fri 65). 4-5's Apply problem is about percentages of a puzzle stock, so this artwork belongs to no current word problem — the data shape suits a Unit 2 statistics question. Predates the 2026-08-14 experience pass. Needs an owner: wire it to a lesson that wants it, or retire it.

Hot dogs labelled '10 count' beside buns labelled '8 count' — an exact match for 6-7's Apply problem, which states hot dogs come in packs of 10 and buns in packs of 8. The artwork was produced and never wired: revealWordProblem carries a title and text but no image field. Ready to wire; held back only because adding it changes what students see, which is an authoring call, not a QA one.
